Dart Basics: Dart is a client-optimized language with sound null safety, type inference, and async/await. It compiles either ahead-of-time or just-in-time.
Widgets: Everything in Flutter is a widget. StatelessWidget builds immutable UI, while StatefulWidget manages mutable state that can trigger rebuilds.
class MyWidget extends StatelessWidget { @override Widget build(BuildContext context) { return Text('Hello'); } }
MaterialApp: MaterialApp wraps your app with Material Design conventions, including theming, navigation, and localization. It provides Scaffold and other Material widgets.
MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')), body: Center(child: Text('Hello'))))

Row: Row arranges child widgets horizontally. It uses MainAxisAlignment for horizontal alignment and CrossAxisAlignment for vertical alignment.
Column: Column arranges child widgets vertically with support for scrolling via Expanded and Flexible widgets for proportional sizing.
Stack: Stack overlays children on top of each other, positioning them with Positioned widget relative to the stack edges.
Stack(children: [Container(color: Colors.blue), Positioned(top: 10, left: 10, child: Text('Overlay'))])
Container: Container combines painting, positioning, and sizing widgets. It supports padding, margins, borders, background color, and constraints.
Container(padding: EdgeInsets.all(16), color: Colors.white, child: Text('Content'))

setState: setState is the simplest state management approach, notifying the framework to rebuild the widget tree when state changes inside StatefulWidget.
Provider: Provider exposes values down the widget tree via InheritedWidget. It is the recommended simple state management solution for Flutter apps.
Provider<Counter>(create: (_) => Counter(), child: Consumer<Counter>(builder: (ctx, counter, _) => Text('${counter.value}')))
Riverpod: Riverpod improves on Provider with compile-time safety, no BuildContext dependency, and support for async providers and code generation.
Bloc: Bloc separates business logic from UI using streams of events and states. It enforces unidirectional data flow and testability.
class CounterCubit extends Cubit<int> { void increment() => emit(state + 1); }

Routes: Named routes map string identifiers to widget builders. Navigator.push and Navigator.pop handle stack-based navigation.
Navigator: Navigator 2.0 provides declarative routing with pages list, allowing deep linking and full control over the navigation stack.
GoRouter: GoRouter provides declarative, URL-based routing with support for deep linking, redirects, and nested navigation using ShellRoute.

Form: Form widget groups form fields for validation and saving. It uses a GlobalKey to access form state and validate all fields at once.

final formKey = GlobalKey<FormState>();
Form(key: formKey, child: Column(children: [TextFormField()]))
TextFormField: TextFormField is a Material Design text input with built-in validation, error display, and controller access for programmatic manipulation.
Validation: Form validation uses validator callbacks that return error strings or null. AutovalidateMode controls when validation triggers.
TextFormField(autovalidateMode: AutovalidateMode.onUserInteraction, validator: (v) => v.length < 3 ? 'Too short' : null)

http: The http package provides a simple, stream-based HTTP client for making REST API calls. It returns Response objects with status codes and bodies.
dio: Dio is a powerful HTTP client with interceptors, request cancellation, timeout handling, and file download/upload progress tracking.
REST API: REST APIs are consumed by mapping JSON responses to Dart models using fromJson/toJson methods. jsonDecode parses raw JSON strings.

final json = jsonDecode(response.body);
final user = User.fromJson(json);
GraphQL: GraphQL queries request specific fields from the server, reducing over-fetching. The graphql_flutter package integrates with the widget tree.
final result = await client.query(QueryOptions(document: gql('{ users { name email } }')));

SharedPreferences: SharedPreferences stores simple key-value pairs persistently. It is platform-native, backed by NSUserDefaults on iOS and SharedPreferences on Android.
SQLite: SQLite provides relational local storage via the sqflite package. Tables are created with SQL and queried using raw or helper methods.
final db = await openDatabase('mydb.db', version: 1, onCreate: (db, v) => db.execute('CREATE TABLE items(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT)'));
Hive: Hive is a lightweight, NoSQL key-value database written in Dart. It is fast and supports type adapters for complex objects.

Platform Channels: Platform channels enable bidirectional communication between Dart and native Kotlin/Swift code via MethodChannel for platform-specific features.
iOS/Android Specific: Platform-specific code uses dart:io Platform checks or conditional imports to handle OS differences in UI, permissions, and behavior.
if (Platform.isIOS) { /* iOS code */ } else if (Platform.isAndroid) { /* Android code */ }
Web: Flutter Web compiles Dart to JavaScript and renders via CanvasKit or HTML renderers. Responsive layouts use LayoutBuilder and MediaQuery for breakpoints.
LayoutBuilder(builder: (ctx, constraints) { if (constraints.maxWidth > 600) return WideLayout(); else return NarrowLayout(); })
